newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador counts corn crop losses from El Nino.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador counts corn crop losses from El Nino.

text.p: Salvadoran farm authorities estimated on Monday that initial corn crop losses from a drop in rainfall because of the impact of El Nino will be almost 2 million 100-lb bags.

According to a report from the Agriculture Ministry, the tiny Central American nation will now produce around 11.6 million bags, or quintals as they are known locally, down from the 13.5 million bags originally forecast.
In the 1996-1997 harvest, El Salvador produced 11.7 million bags.

The revised output forecast came from the ministry's estimate that 249,261 hectares were planted with corn this cycle and that 99,570 hectares have been damaged by the low rainfall, especially in the west and east of El Salvador.
El Nino is a weather system that warms seas in the South Pacific and throws global weather patterns into turmoil.
El Salvador's rice and sorghum crops have also been hit, but to a lesser degree, the ministry said. No details were given.

The country is traditionally a net importer of grains. In the 1996 calendar year, El Salvador imported 369,800 tonnes of corn, sorghum, dry beans and rice. In 1995, imports of the same grains totaled 322,100 tonnes, according to the Farm Economy Department of the Agriculture Ministry.

Authorities have already announced measures to facilitate private sector imports of grains to make up the deficit. No details of the import aid have been given. One government report outlined that the government is going to "consider purchase options (of corn) in international markets".

Last week, Agriculture Minister Ricardo Quinonez said the government was willing to facilitate imports of 1.5 million quintals of corn and dry beans this cycle because of foreseen shortages. He gave no breakdown.
El Salvador last week predicted the country's total grains harvest for 1997-1998 would be down 10-12 percent from the originally forecast 22.1 million quintals because of El Nino.
